trap-superlative.evidence: 'quantifies the 80$\times$ gap closure for ${}^4_2He$' overstates the cited witness by a factor of ~6. The witness's own honest_gap_report says 'closing the alpha_shift gap by 13.5x (
trap-superlative.notes: rel_err| 0.7904 -> 0.0587)', and I recomputed 0.7904/0.0587 = 13.47. The '80' looks like the alpha-shift miss of -79%% (a percentage) re-read as a factor.|proposed: 'quantifies the 13.5x gap closure for ${}^4_2He$ (|rel_err| 0.7904 -> 0.0587)'. Numeric, so flagged rather than edited.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: THREE literal instances of the corpus's named token substitution, two of them leaving broken sentences. (1) 'sourced from the canonical / the canonical formalism / entry `2·m_e·4·Vol(L6a4)`' — the phrase is duplicated across two lines and the sentence has no grammatical subject for 'entry'. (2) A section header reading '## canonical witness' — a bare lowercase 'canonical' opening, the documented tell. (3) 'the canonical formalism / emits a comparison witness showing…' — a formalism does not emit a witness; a producer does, and here it is identifiable as computations/binding_alpha_shift_witness.py, which the cited witness JSON names in its own 'generator' field.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: proposed: (1) '…sourced from the canonical magic_A_formula.magic_A_binding entry `2·m_e·4·Vol(L6a4)`' (the witness's magic_A_inputs.source names exactly this); (2) '## Comparison witness'; (3) '`computations/binding_alpha_shift_witness.py` emits a comparison witness…'. Flagged rather than fixed: (1) is grammatically broken in a way that needs the author to confirm the intended referent.
